source: Canonical legacy identities 101-125 in data/v2-audit/current-question-audit.json order.

expansion_backlog_changes.core_trait_gap: drains and frustrations anchored in governed motivations
expansion_backlog_changes.motivational_tradeoff: which obstruction to progress, possibility, trust, or clarity most reliably reduces energy
expansion_backlog_changes.insufficiency: Legacy drain and frustration items rely on boredom, tension, bluntness, anxiety, or accountability virtues rather than showing which governed motivation is blocked.

current.prompt: I feel best about earning money when it helps support people I care about.

proposed.prompt: Earning more feels most meaningful to me when it strengthens security or support for people I care about rather than mainly expanding my own options.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: supporting people and continuity vs. expanding personal options
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether relational support gives earning greater meaning than expanded personal options.

questions.why: The revision creates a real motivational contrast and measures Yellow support without implying that earning for oneself is selfish.

current.prompt: I’m usually the one suggesting plans or activities when people are hanging out.

proposed.prompt: When friends have free time and no plan, I’m often drawn to introduce a new activity rather than continue with whatever is already familiar.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: new shared possibility vs. familiar social continuity
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether introducing a new shared possibility feels more natural than continuing a familiar activity.

questions.why: Suggesting plans alone can reflect Red initiative; the revision makes Blue novelty and shared experience the reason for acting.

current.prompt: In a group project, I’m most likely to…

options.wording: take the lead and set the pace
keep the energy up and rally people
organize the plan and track details

proposed.prompt: A newly formed team needs a way of working together. What would you most naturally help establish first?

options.label: Clear ownership for decisions and the pace needed to deliver
An open exchange where possibilities and energy can build
Shared expectations that support trust and dependable commitments
Defined roles, processes, and checkpoints that keep work coherent

replacement.prompt: A newly formed team needs a way of working together. What would you most naturally help establish first?

options.wording: Clear ownership for decisions and the pace needed to deliver
An open exchange where possibilities and energy can build
Shared expectations that support trust and dependable commitments
Defined roles, processes, and checkpoints that keep work coherent

option_to_color.wording: Clear ownership for decisions and the pace needed to deliver
An open exchange where possibilities and energy can build
Shared expectations that support trust and dependable commitments
Defined roles, processes, and checkpoints that keep work coherent

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: direction vs. possibility exchange vs. trust and support vs. dependable process
measurement.what_it_measures: Which useful working foundation someone naturally helps establish in a newly formed team.

questions.why: The legacy options are leadership stereotypes and make Yellow uniquely inclusive; the candidate provides four competent team foundations.

current.prompt: I’m uncomfortable when money becomes the main focus over people.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: financial focus vs. attention to people
measurement.what_it_measures: Discomfort when money receives more attention than people.

questions.why: The item frames money focus as morally suspect and does not expose a governed Yellow relational motivation or balanced alternative.

current.prompt: I’m comfortable making decisions even when I don’t have all the information.

proposed.prompt: If a decision can be changed later, I’d rather choose a workable option now than wait for every detail.

replacement.prompt: If a decision can be changed later, I’d rather choose a workable option now than wait for every detail.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: reversible decision and momentum vs. complete detail
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether choosing a reversible workable option feels preferable to waiting for every detail.

questions.why: Comfort with missing information can reflect risk tolerance or Blue spontaneity; the candidate ties the choice to Red momentum and reversibility.

current.prompt: I’m usually up for trying something new if it sounds fun.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: fun new experience vs. familiar option
measurement.what_it_measures: Willingness to try something new when it sounds enjoyable.

questions.why: The item is broad and duplicates stronger discovery, unpredictable-experience, and shared-novelty questions without adding a distinct motive or context.

current.prompt: At a party or club, you’ll find me…

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: status area vs. dance floor vs. familiar people vs. observation
measurement.what_it_measures: Typical physical or social position at a party or club.

questions.why: VIP status, dancing, staying close, and hanging back are cultural or situational stereotypes rather than governed color motivations.

current.prompt: I enjoy social situations when there’s a clear purpose or activity involved.

proposed.prompt: At a social gathering, I’m more engaged when the group is working toward a shared outcome than when the main purpose is conversation itself.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: shared outcome vs. conversation as the primary experience
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether a shared outcome makes social participation more engaging than conversation alone.

questions.why: A clear purpose can attract any color; the revision makes Red outcome orientation the explicit social discriminator.

current.prompt: I pay attention to who might feel left out during group activities.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: inclusive attention vs. activity momentum
measurement.what_it_measures: Attention to who might be excluded during group activity.

questions.why: Noticing exclusion is socially desirable and can reflect fairness or learned facilitation; the item does not reveal why belonging matters to Yellow.

current.prompt: I trust myself to adapt if things don’t go as planned.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: confidence in adaptation vs. advance control
measurement.what_it_measures: Confidence in personal ability to adapt after plans fail.

questions.why: Adaptability and confidence are learned competencies available to every color and are not independent Red evidence.

current.prompt: I feel more confident when I know there’s a plan backing my actions.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: plan-backed confidence vs. action without plan
measurement.what_it_measures: Confidence gained from having a plan behind one’s actions.

questions.why: The statement measures confidence and repeats stronger planning-versus-flexibility items already proposed.

current.prompt: In meetings, I’m usually the one who…

options.wording: makes sure quieter people are heard

proposed.prompt: A discussion has produced useful input but still needs a practical next step. What do you most naturally contribute first?

options.label: Name the decision needed and move the group toward it
Connect the ideas into possibilities the group can build on
Check which direction people can support and sustain together
Clarify the evidence, open questions, and decision criteria

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: decision and momentum vs. connected possibilities vs. sustainable support vs. evidence and criteria
measurement.what_it_measures: Which contribution someone makes first after useful group input still needs a next step.

questions.why: The revision removes stories, inclusion, and questions as color stereotypes and makes each option a useful decision contribution.

current.prompt: I feel closest to people I can be myself around without overthinking.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: unselfconscious expression vs. guarded interaction
measurement.what_it_measures: Closeness with people around whom self-expression feels effortless.

questions.why: Feeling safe to be oneself can indicate trust, maturity, context, or either Blue expression or Yellow relational safety; the assignment is not discriminating.

current.prompt: I lose steam when things feel routine or predictable for too long.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: variety vs. predictable routine
measurement.what_it_measures: Loss of energy during prolonged routine or predictability.

questions.why: The item defines Blue through inability to sustain routine, directly violating the approved deficit-framing rule and duplicating stronger positive freedom items.

current.prompt: I value honesty more than keeping the peace.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: honesty vs. harmony
measurement.what_it_measures: Stated preference for honesty over interpersonal peace.

questions.why: Honesty is a universal virtue and the contrast makes harmony sound dishonest; directness alone is not Red evidence.

current.prompt: I tend to slow down decisions if I sense tension or discomfort between people.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: interpersonal comfort vs. decision speed
measurement.what_it_measures: Slowing decisions in response to interpersonal tension.

questions.why: This is an exact duplicate of Question 64, already replaced by the governed C02-L-Y-01 trust-versus-closure candidate.

current.prompt: I enjoy social situations more when there’s a goal, game, or outcome involved.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: goal-oriented social activity vs. open social interaction
measurement.what_it_measures: Greater enjoyment of social situations containing a goal, game, or outcome.

questions.why: This duplicates Question 108’s semantic family; Question 108 receives the clearer motive-centered revision.

current.prompt: I’m uncomfortable when people are treated unfairly or excluded.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: fair inclusion vs. unfair exclusion
measurement.what_it_measures: Emotional discomfort with unfair or exclusionary treatment.

questions.why: Fairness and inclusion are universal ethical positions and explicitly cannot independently score Yellow.

current.prompt: I lose respect when people avoid accountability.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: accountability vs. avoidance
measurement.what_it_measures: Loss of respect for people who avoid accountability.

questions.why: Accountability is a universal virtue and avoidance is pejorative; the item does not distinguish Red responsibility for results from mature behavior available to all colors.

current.prompt: I prefer a boss who…

proposed.prompt: A supervisor gives you meaningful autonomy. Which quality most helps you do your best work?

options.label: They define an ambitious result and give me authority to pursue it
They welcome new ideas and leave room to adapt the approach
They build a dependable working relationship and protect shared commitments
They explain the criteria, evidence, and constraints behind expectations

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: ambitious result vs. adaptive possibility vs. dependable relationship vs. explained criteria
measurement.what_it_measures: Which supervisor quality most supports a person’s natural motivation under meaningful autonomy.

questions.why: The revision preserves valuable preference-in-others coverage while replacing push, positivity, caring, and instruction stereotypes with balanced foundations.

current.prompt: I prefer stability over taking chances when outcomes are uncertain.

proposed.prompt: I prefer stability over taking chances when outcomes are uncertain.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: stability vs. uncertain opportunity
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether stability is preferred to taking chances under uncertain outcomes.

questions.why: The item states a legitimate Green risk preference with a clear opportunity cost and does not rely on anxiety or generic competence.

current.prompt: With deadlines, I…

options.wording: race the clock and finish strong
start late but bring big energy
check in so nobody gets stuck

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: racing vs. late energy vs. helping others vs. early preparation
measurement.what_it_measures: Self-described behavior while working toward deadlines.

questions.why: The Blue option admits procrastination, Red implies rushing, and the remaining options claim helpfulness or discipline; the item measures work habits and competence stereotypes.

current.prompt: I’d rather avoid risk than deal with potential complications later.

proposed.prompt: When an uncertain option offers meaningful upside, I prefer identifying likely complications and safeguards before committing rather than handling problems only if they appear.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: risk controls before commitment vs. handling complications if they arise
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether identifying complications and safeguards precedes commitment to uncertain upside.

questions.why: The revision replaces avoidance with positive Green risk control and acknowledges that the uncertain option has legitimate upside.

current.prompt: I’m willing to compromise on speed if it helps maintain trust.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: trust maintenance vs. speed
measurement.what_it_measures: Willingness to accept slower progress to maintain trust.

questions.why: This is an exact duplicate of Question 43, already approved as KEEP_EXACTLY.

current.prompt: What drains me fastest?

proposed.prompt: Which situation most quickly reduces your energy?

options.label: Progress remains stalled even after a direction has been chosen
The experience becomes fixed with no room for a new possibility
A shared commitment continues while trust or connection erodes
Important decisions proceed without clear evidence or criteria

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: stalled progress vs. fixed experience vs. eroding trust vs. unsupported decisions
measurement.what_it_measures: Which obstruction to a governed core motivation most quickly reduces energy.

questions.why: The revision retains valuable drain/frustration coverage while replacing boredom, tension, and unclear expectations with governed motivational obstructions.
